14	CASE OD2-HO-CONTRA-1 (CONTRA, organizational): Corran Valley Medical Centre: a 26-week slip and a claim due on 1 December
15	Setting: Callerby Construct is a regional general contractor. It built Corran Valley Medical Centre, a four-storey steel-frame medical building, for the developer Halden Medical Properties under a £14.6m contract. The contract completion date was 30 April 2026. Practical completion came on 29 October 2026. Halden is deducting liquidated damages. Callerby's project director and a claims consultant have drafted a claim that blames the delay on Halden. Halden blames Callerby. The project's lender appointed an independent monitoring surveyor, and the project ran its information requests (RFIs) through a shared platform hosted by a third party. Callerby's Northern region also delivered Kestrel, a distribution warehouse, over the same period.
16	Presenting request: Callerby's chief executive wants to know what actually caused the Corran Valley slip, and what Callerby should do about the drafted extension-of-time and prolongation claim, which is due to go to Halden on 1 December. She also wants to know what should happen inside the company.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Email from Ruth Abernethy, chief executive, Callerby Construct, 12 Nov 2026 (leadership-account): 'Corran Valley Medical Centre reached practical completion on 29 October, 26 weeks after the contract date of 30 April. Halden is withholding £1.17m in liquidated damages. Our extension-of-time and prolongation claim for £1.9m is due to go to Halden on 1 December. Gareth says the slip is down to Halden's design changes and their architect's slow answers; Halden says the opposite. Before I sign anything I need to know what actually drove the slip and what we do next. On a brighter note, the Northern region had a good year: Kestrel warehouse handed over seven weeks early in March, and the regional early-handover incentive paid out to Colm Faraday's team.'
19	E2 [stage S1] Interview notes, Gareth Imrie, project director, 4 Nov 2026 (manager-account): Says Halden 'redesigned the building while we were building it'. Cites six change orders, CO-07 to CO-12, including CO-09, which moved the MRI suite to level 2. Halden flagged it in September and it needed extra steel. 'We couldn't carry on with the frame until CO-09 was resolved, and the architect sat on our steel connection queries for weeks.' Confirms the tower crane went to the Kestrel job in October: 'Kestrel's hired crane failed its thorough examination, the region needed one, and ours was standing idle anyway. Colm and I agreed it.' Says he has 'had a word' with the site superintendent about 'chatting to Halden's clerk of works'.
20	E3 [stage S1] Draft claim summary, Fenmore Claims Advisory, prepared for Callerby, 28 Oct 2026 (document): The time impact analysis attributes the full 26-week delay to employer risk events: (a) owner change orders CO-07 to CO-12, issued 12 Sep–9 Dec 2025 and holding the structural frame: 17 weeks; (b) late information: 41 of 64 RFIs, including structural connection queries, open longer than the contractual response period: a further 9 weeks. RFI durations come from the 'created' date in the project RFI log. Programme inputs are the contractor's monthly updates. Claimed: a 26-week extension of time and £1.9m in prolongation costs. Engagement terms: Fenmore's fee includes 6% of sums recovered.
21	E4 [stage S1] Letter, Priya Varma, development manager, Halden Medical Properties, to Callerby, 10 Nov 2026 (customer-account): 'We understand a delay claim is being prepared, so please note our position now. Your tower crane left site in October 2025 and did not come back until April. Your own superintendent told our clerk of works it had gone to another of your jobs. Our architect answered your queries promptly. The change orders concerned interior layouts and were small.' Halden will deduct liquidated damages in full and reserves its right to recover its own extra consultant and finance costs from Callerby.
22	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Dale Pruitt, site superintendent, 5 Nov 2026 (staff-account): 'Autumn and winter were dead. The crane and the frame gang went over to Kestrel and we did bits: drainage, level 1 blockwork.' Asked why: 'Above my pay grade. Gareth and Colm sorted it.' Asked whether levels 3–4 could have gone up: 'Steel was on the ground. Whether every connection query was answered, I couldn't swear to; that's Gareth's side.' Recalls that steel deliveries for levels 1–2 were 'all over the place in the summer'. Confirms he told Halden's clerk of works where the crane had gone: 'He asked. I wasn't going to lie.'
23	E6 [stage S1] Callerby monthly progress report no. 14 to Halden, November 2025, signed G. Imrie (document): 'Frame: level 3–4 erection resequenced pending resolution of CO-09 structural information and outstanding connection queries. Tower crane temporarily demobilised to reduce standing costs during the design hold.' The programme update moves frame completion from 19 Dec 2025 to 'TBC – subject to CO-09'. Stated critical path: CO-09 design → frame → envelope → fit-out. The report does not yet claim any change to the contract completion date.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Halden Medical Properties board minutes, July–December 2025 - Halden Medical Properties company secretary (document): Extracts supplied by Halden. 22 Jul 2025: the board approves in principle moving the MRI suite from the ground floor to level 2; the architect is to advise on structure and cost. 16 Sep: approves a CO-09 budget of £212,000; the development manager is to notify the contractor. 18 Nov: notes the contractor's monthly report, which attributes the frame hold to CO-09; the development manager is 'to monitor and reserve position'. 9 Dec: approves CO-12, level 4 joinery, £38,000. No other programme discussion is recorded.
26	C2 [stage S1] Callerby plant ledger, tower crane TC-3, July 2025–June 2026 - Callerby finance system (financial-record): Internal hire charges for company tower crane TC-3. Corran Valley cost code: 1 Jul–19 Oct 2025 and 31 Mar–26 Jun 2026. Kestrel warehouse cost code: 23 Oct 2025–20 Mar 2026. Dismantling, transport and re-erection charges (£46,800) were posted to Corran Valley. The 'approved by' field reads 'regional office' for both transfers. No transfer request forms are attached to the ledger.
27	C3 [stage S1] Public weather station summary, October 2025–April 2026 - Nearest public weather station, 6 km from site (external-data): Rainfall for the period was 94% of the 30-year average. 28	C4 [stage S1] Lender's monitoring surveyor reports, October 2025–April 2026 - Pell & Rowe, monitoring surveyor to Ashlow Commercial Bank (independent-observation): Pell & Rowe, monitoring surveyor to Ashlow Commercial Bank (Halden's lender); monthly reports, copied to both parties. 15 Oct 2025: frame on programme; level 3–4 steel delivered 6–14 Oct, stored on site; erection programmed from 21 Oct. 18 Nov: tower crane dismantled 20–22 Oct, 'required on another company project' per contractor; no erection since. CO-09 issued 6 Nov: four infill beams, level 2 only. 16 Dec: CO-09 beams installed 8–12 Dec using hired mobile crane; levels 3–4 untouched. Jan–Mar: no tower crane, no erection. 14 Apr 2026: crane re-erected 1–3 Apr; level 3 erection resumed 6 Apr. Completion forecast now 29 Oct 2026: frame delay plus cladding contractor's next slot (May). COs 07, 08, 10–12 are fit-out, not started, within float. Contractor's monthly factual-accuracy response: 'no comments'.
29	C5 [stage S1] Corran Valley site daily diaries, 20 October 2025–10 April 2026 - Callerby site office (log): Typed by the assistant project manager and countersigned by the project director. 21 Oct: 'TC-3 dismantle. Frame on hold – design (CO-09).' Every entry from 22 Oct to 3 Apr repeats 'Frame: on hold – design', with daily labour of 9–14 (groundworks, drainage, level 1 blockwork). 10 Dec: 'Mobile crane – misc lifts.' 6 Apr: 'L3 steel erection commenced.' No entry says which design information was outstanding or when any of it arrived.
30	C6 [stage S1] Architect's change order register, CO-01 to CO-14 - Lindqvist Okafor Architects, for Halden (document): The register lists 14 change orders with issue date, title and value. CO-07 (12 Sep 2025): level 4 partition layout, £61k. CO-08 (30 Sep): level 2 waiting area, £24k. CO-09 (6 Nov): MRI relocation, structural and M&E, £212k. CO-10 (14 Nov): level 2 nurse base, £17k. CO-11 (28 Nov): data cabling, £44k. CO-12 (9 Dec): level 4 joinery, £38k. The register contains no programme or time assessment.
31	C7 [stage S1] Callerby HR records, Corran Valley site management team, 2025–2026 - Callerby HR system (system-record): Site management team: project director, project manager, two site engineers, superintendent and assistant project manager. The project manager resigned in January 2026 and a replacement started in February 2026. Overtime, sickness absence and training hours were within company norms. One grievance was logged, about site parking, and resolved. No disciplinary records for the period.
32	C8 [stage S1] Tarrant Façades correspondence with Callerby, December 2025–May 2026 - Tarrant Façades, cladding subcontractor (vendor-account): 4 Dec 2025: 'We cannot start in January as programmed; the frame is incomplete. Please confirm a revised date.' 19 Feb 2026: 'Still no frame completion date. Our crews will be committed elsewhere until May.' 2 May 2026: confirms mobilisation and asks for £28,000 for remobilisation and the lost slot. The letters do not say why the frame was incomplete.
33	C9 [stage S1] Shared RFI platform export with audit timestamps, all project RFIs - Project RFI platform, hosted by an independent software provider (system-record): Users cannot edit the platform's audit trail. All 64 RFIs are included, each with 'created' (contractor draft opened), 'submitted' and 'answered' timestamps. Measured from submission, the architect's median response was 4 working days, and 62 of 64 were answered within the 10-working-day contract period. The two exceptions are RFI-052 (12 days) and RFI-058 (11 days), both on level 2 ceiling finishes in May 2026; the contractor marked both 'no programme impact' when submitting. Of the 41 RFIs the draft claim lists as late, 39 sat in contractor draft status for 9–47 days before submission. Structural RFIs, Oct 2025–Apr 2026: RFI-029 (submitted 2 Oct, answered 7 Oct), RFI-031 on CO-09 connections (10 Nov, 14 Nov), RFI-036 (28 Jan, 30 Jan).
34	C10 [stage S1] Corran Valley health and safety incident register, January 2025–October 2026 - Callerby safety system (system-record): Fourteen entries: nine first-aid cases; three near-misses, including a slewing incident during the 10 Dec 2025 mobile crane lift; and two reportable injuries during fit-out in August 2026 (a slip and a hand laceration). Each entry was closed with investigation notes. No regulator enforcement action is recorded.
35	C11 [stage S1] Fenmore Claims Advisory time impact analysis workbook - Fenmore Claims Advisory (expert-account): The workbook behind the draft claim. Baseline: programme revision 3 (March 2025). Progress inputs: Callerby monthly programme updates nos. 12–24, as supplied by the project director. Delay fragments were inserted for CO-07 to CO-12 using the dates in the monthly reports, and for 'information delay' using RFI 'created' to 'answered' durations. Plant and crane availability are not modelled. Analyst note: 'Third-party contemporaneous records not reviewed; not supplied by client.'
36	C12 [stage S1] Callerby internal close-out report, Kestrel distribution warehouse, March 2026 - Callerby Northern region (document): Handover on 13 Mar 2026, seven weeks ahead of contract. The client paid no early-completion bonus. The regional early-handover incentive was triggered for the Northern region team. Lifting: the hired crane was withdrawn after failing its thorough examination on 9 Oct 2025; company crane TC-3 was brought in from Corran Valley and erected 23–25 Oct. Lessons learned: 'secure backup crane options at tender stage.'
37	C13 [stage S1] Callerby anonymous staff survey 2026, Northern region results - Callerby HR, survey provider summary (anonymous-staff-survey): Response rate 58% (n=112). 'Resources are allocated fairly between projects': 31% agree (company 52%). 'I can raise programme concerns without fear': 44% agree (company 61%). Common free-text themes include 'targets' and 'pressure to hand over'. No breakdown by project is available.
38	C14 [stage S1] Local authority building control inspection records, Corran Valley - Local authority building control (regulator-record): Inspections were recorded for foundations (March 2025), drainage (April 2025) and fire stopping (August–September 2026). A completion certificate was issued on 27 Oct 2026. No frame-stage inspections are recorded, because the structural frame was certified by the contractor's engineer.
39	C15 [stage S1] Callerby group internal audit report on plant utilisation, February 2025 - Callerby group internal audit (prior-report): Average tower crane utilisation across the group was 71%. Regional directors allocate cranes between projects with no group-level check on programme impact. The audit recommended central plant scheduling. Management response: 'Agreed, target Q4 2025.' Status in October 2026: not implemented.
40	CANDIDATES
41	H1: Owner-directed design changes held up critical-path work.
42	H2: Late responses from the owner's architect to the contractor's information requests held up critical-path work.
43	H3: The contractor's redeployment of its own equipment or crews to other work held up critical-path work.
44	H4: Late delivery of structural steel by the fabricator held up critical-path work.
45	R1: Tower crane absent from the Corran Valley site, October 2025 to April 2026 -> Late completion of the structural frame (caused)
46	R2: Owner change orders CO-07 to CO-12 -> Late completion of the structural frame (caused)
47	R3: Architect RFI responses exceeding the contractual response period -> Late completion of the structural frame (caused)
48	R4: Regional early-handover incentive scheme -> Decision to move the tower crane to the Kestrel project (caused)
49	A1: Submit the drafted 26-week extension-of-time and prolongation claim to Halden on 1 December as drafted.
50	A2: Withdraw the drafted claim and settle the final account with Halden on the basis that the frame stoppage was Callerby's own responsibility.
51	A3: Suspend the regional early-handover incentive scheme on the grounds that it drove the crane transfer.
52	A4: Commission a second claims consultant to prepare an independent forensic delay analysis before deciding whether to submit any claim.
53	A5: Issue the site superintendent a formal written warning for discussing the crane's whereabouts with Halden's clerk of works.
54	SCORED ITEMS
55	Q1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
56	Q2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
57	Q3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
58	Q4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
59	Q5: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
60	Q6: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
61	Q7: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
62	Q8: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
63	Q9: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
64	Q10: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
65	Q11: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
66	Q12: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
67	Q13: action A5 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
68	Q14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

answers.justification: CO-09 was issued on 6 Nov, after the crane was dismantled on 20–22 Oct. It added only four level-2 infill beams, which were fitted 8–12 Dec, and levels 3–4 were not touched until April (C4, C6). The other change orders were fit-out work within float (C4), and the related RFI-031 was answered in 4 days (C9).

The tamper-proof platform audit shows 62 of 64 RFIs answered within the contract period, measured from submission. The two late ones were ceiling-finish queries in May 2026 that Callerby itself marked 'no programme impact'. The structural RFIs took 2–5 days (C9). The claim's 'late' durations count days the RFIs sat as contractor drafts (C9, C11).

Level 3–4 steel was on site and erection was programmed from 21 Oct. The crane then left for Kestrel, and erection stopped until it returned in April (C4, C2, C12, E5). Callerby's own monthly factual-accuracy response raised 'no comments' (C4).

The monitoring surveyor recorded the frame on programme on 15 Oct, with level 3–4 steel delivered 6–14 Oct and stored on site (C4, E5). The only hint of late steel is the summer level 1–2 deliveries (E5), and nothing shows they affected completion.

The crane left on 20–22 Oct and frame erection stopped. It came back on 1–3 Apr and erection resumed on 6 Apr. Steel was on site, and the rival design and RFI explanations are ruled out by independent records (C4, C9, C2, C12).
CO-07, 08 and 10–12 were fit-out items within float. CO-09 affected only level-2 infill beams, which were finished by 12 Dec, while levels 3–4 stayed idle for lack of a crane (C4, C6).

Measured from submission, the structural RFIs were answered within 2–5 days. The only responses outside the contract period came in May 2026, had no programme impact, and fell after the frame period (C9).

The incentive paid out to the team that received the crane, and the survey records 'pressure to hand over' (E1, C12, C13). However, Kestrel's own crane failing its examination explains the transfer on its own (C12, E2), and no record shows the incentive motivated the decision (C2 has no transfer forms).

Submitting a 26-week claim that independent records contradict (C4, C9, C11) would put Callerby on record with a misleading claim. Callerby's own progress reports and its 'no comments' response would expose it (E6, C4), and Halden is already reserving its own costs (E4).

The frame stoppage is shown to be Callerby's own responsibility (C4, C2, C9, C12), so withdrawing the claim and settling on that basis matches the evidence. Legitimate change-order valuations can still go through the final account (C6).

The incentive's role in the crane transfer is not established, because the failed Kestrel crane is a sufficient alternative explanation (C12). The documented control gap is that regional directors allocate cranes with no group-level check, flagged by the 2025 audit and still unfixed (C15).

An independent analysis is reasonable given Fenmore's 6% success fee and its unreviewed inputs (E3, C11). But the third-party records (C4, C9) already settle the main question, so another study is not needed before dropping the claim.

The superintendent truthfully answered a direct question from the clerk of works (E5), and Callerby's own report had already told Halden about the demobilisation (E6). A warning would punish honesty and discourage people from raising issues, in a region where staff already report fear of raising programme concerns (C13).

Independent, tamper-proof and internal financial records all agree that the crane's redeployment caused the stoppage and that the design and RFI causes did not (C4, C9, C2, C12, C5). That is enough to commit to withdrawing the claim and settling.
